summary: Appalachian Trail lookout on Wesser Bald in the Nantahala Forest; cab burned in 1979, observation deck since the early 1990s; built 1936 or 1934, sources differ.

facts.design: Live-in cab with catwalk on a metal tower; the cab was replaced by a viewing platform (observation deck)

access.note: The Appalachian Trail goes by the tower, and the deck is an observation deck for hikers. Undated sources; no 2025-26 notice found.

visit.trail_note: About 1.5 miles on the Appalachian Trail from Tellico Gap, with about 767 feet of elevation gain; Tellico Gap has unimproved road access.

events.note: A 1934 USGS survey note places a benchmark in a new lookout tower; conflicts with the register's 1936 date
Register's Built field: a metal tower with a live-in cab. Willhite says the CCC built a 30-foot tower with live-in cab
Earl Shaffer spent a night in the tower during his thru-hike, per Willhite
Register says burned by vandals; Willhite says the cab was destroyed by arson
Register: cab replaced with a viewing platform in 1993; Willhite says early 1990s
Registered April 2, 2008; nominated by Peter J. Barr
Repairs in summer 2008 by chapter member Charles Nuckolls: wooden stairs, railings and deck flooring replaced
Reported destroyed in the November 2016 Nantahala Forest fires, later found to have survived (Wikipedia)

notes_for_editor: Built year is disputed: the register says 1936 and Willhite cites a 1934 USGS benchmark note, so both are kept as events. Burn cause differs: register says vandals, Willhite says arson. Material differs: register says metal, Wikipedia says wooden. Deck date: register says 1993, Willhite says early 1990s. The 2016 fire line rests on Wikipedia alone; a Forest Service or news source would strengthen it. Access and climbability come from undated sources. The record's height_m 9.0 (OSM) is close to the register's 30 ft, so it is left as is. The 1948 Shaffer detail is from Willhite only. The story no longer says the observation deck exists today: the only source is undated, so it is attributed to Willhite.
